examiner (exam-1): approach for `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_amendments.mjs`.

Reading of the legs, and how each is driven:

- (a) [M1] static: import `IMPLEMENTER_SCHEMA` from `../run-engine.mjs` and read `properties.amendments` — `type: 'array'`, `items.required` sorted deep-equal `['amends','what','why']`, `items.properties.amends.enum` deep-equal `['clause','files','sim']` (order-pinned, the leg says deep-equal), and the schema's own `required` deep-equal `['status','summary','startHead']`. A stub reply is never schema-validated, so this is the only leg that can read the constant; (b)-(f) drive the `noteConcerns` seam with canned replies.
- (b) [M2] one-task wave, `proofRuns: ["sh -c 'echo green'"]`, implementer returns DONE + two amendments (`files` then `sim`). Reads `events.jsonl` (split/parse/drop-blanks, copied not imported), asserts exactly two `driver:amendment` lines, each `{task, amends, what, why}` verbatim + string `id` + numeric `ts`, in reply order, both at a lower index than the task's first `driver:proof-run`.
- (c) [M2] red-then-fixed `proofRuns`: the command is `sh -c 'cat fixed.txt'`, red for the implementer (file absent) and green once the `fix:<id>:0` stub writes it. Implementer declares none, fix declares one `{amends: 'clause'}`: exactly one `driver:amendment`, at a HIGHER index than the first `driver:proof-run`, and exactly one `amendment (` judgmentCalls line.
- (d) [M2] leg (b)'s run: the `amendment (` judgmentCalls lines deep-equal to the two full expected strings, em dash and all.
- (e) [M3] leg (b)'s `report.amendments` deep-equal to the two rows in order; plus a two-task wave declaring none → key present and deep-equal `[]`.
- (f) [M4] a DONE_WITH_CONCERNS reply with `concerns: ['out-of-FILES (not taken): a.txt — owed']` and no `amendments` key, and the same reply with `amendments: []`: zero `driver:amendment` lines in both, and the concern reaching judgmentCalls verbatim as `task <id>: out-of-FILES (not taken): a.txt — owed`.
- (g) [M5] the Proof's third and fourth `Run:` lines, asked in-process with the same range-then-match semantics: the `^Judgment rules:` paragraph of `fleet/roles/implementer.md` and the `^The same judgment rules` paragraph of `fleet/roles/fix.md`, each read to the next blank line, flattened, matched against the same ordered token sequences.
- (h) [M2] the Proof's second `Run:` line — the whole-suite bridge. A sim may not spawn pytest or another sim, so that leg is the driver's own `Run:` line and is not encodable inside this file; what this file owes it is to BE one of the sims the bridge runs, which it is. Returned under `unsatisfiable` for transparency, not as a coverage gap.

One reading worth recording: `amends` (not `kind`) is asserted as the row's field name in every leg, because `kind` is the event's own type field (`kind: 'driver:amendment'`) — an implementation that named the row field `kind` would collide there, and legs (b), (c), (e) all fail on the field name rather than on the count.

The rig's default is `{"verdict":"PASS"}` (`bootEnv`'s `STUB_VERDICT: 'PASS'`, `_sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs:755,937`), and `do_boot` greens a run only on `verdict = PASS` or an approve receipt (`fleet/sandbox-boot.sh:3410-3424`) — a receipt spelling `green` PARKS the run, and its card opens `**Parked:** parked: gate verdict green`. Legs (a) and (c) both say "the green boot", so the exam sets `{"verdict":"PASS","gateCheck":{"acks":[{"type":"deferred:external","detail":"the deploy waits on a credential"}]}}`, keeping the ack the leg is about. Measured on that receipt at BASE: the card renders `Residuals: 1 from review`, a blank line, one `- deferred:external — the deploy waits on a credential` line, then `<details><summary>Record</summary>` — exactly the neighbourhood M3 and M4 name, with no `Amendments:` line anywhere, which is the one reason the exam is red at BASE.

Second reading: `what`'s newline rides as a JSON `\\n` escape (the report is written `printf '%s\\n' "$STUB_REPORT"`, so a raw newline in the env value makes the document unparsable and every card cell a dash). The exam builds the report as `DEFAULT_REPORT.slice(0, -1) + ',"amendments":' + JSON.stringify(AMENDMENTS) + '}'` and derives the expected card lines from that same array by M3's own rule, so the expectation is the clause applied to the fixture rather than a second copy of it.

The Proof's third `Run:` line greps an ORDERED BRE: `amendments.*files.*clause.*sim.*what.*why.*out-of-FILES (not taken):.*plan-defect: leg (x) cannot pass`. So in `fleet/roles/implementer.md`'s judgment-rules paragraph the amendments sentence must be placed BEFORE the `out-of-FILES (not taken):` sentence, not appended after the `plan-defect:` sentences where it reads most naturally. The first throwaway wording put it last and leg (g) failed on the order alone. What worked at the scratch check: the sentence inserted immediately after `never delete a file outside FILES.`, keeping it one paragraph (no blank line — the range is read by `sed -n '/^Judgment rules:/,/^$/p'`). Note also that a naive find-and-replace on `never delete a file outside FILES.` misses: the paragraph is hard-wrapped with the newline between `never` and `delete`.

A textual insertion of the amendments call keyed on the 4-space form lands at both sites plus the fix site a second time, so a fix reply carrying one amendment appends TWO `driver:amendment` lines. Leg (c)'s `ams.length === 1` is the assertion that catches it — it did, on the first scratch attempt. Anchor each insertion on its own indentation, or call the seam from a single place.

A sim may not spawn `pytest` or another sim, so that leg is the driver's own `Run:` line and is not encodable inside a sim; what this file owes it is to BE one of the sims that bridge collects, which it is. One ambiguity resolved, recorded so the exam's author and any later session read it the same way.

Leg (e) is worded "a review prompt with no \`AMENDMENTS\` substring". Read as a bare substring that is unsatisfiable by construction: the review prompt is \`roles.reviewer + …\`, and M3 (plus five of the Proof's own \`Run:\` legs) REQUIRES the word AMENDMENTS to appear in \`fleet/roles/reviewer.md\`. So the role text always carries it, and no implementation can make the whole prompt free of the bare word while also satisfying M3.

Resolved by M2, which is the authoritative Machine clause: "contains no \`AMENDMENTS:\`" — with the colon. That IS satisfiable and is what I implemented: \`reviewer.md\` never writes AMENDMENTS immediately followed by a colon (it is "AMENDMENTS, when present", "an \`AMENDMENTS\` entry", "in AMENDMENTS,"), so a task whose replies declared none has a prompt with zero \`AMENDMENTS:\` occurrences. I checked the stronger form too: everything the DRIVER assembles (the prompt from \`\\nPATCH: \` onward, i.e. excluding the role prefix) contains no \`AMENDMENTS\` at all when nothing was declared. Both readings hold; only the literal whole-prompt bare-substring reading does not.

This is a disclosure, not a park — the clause it is derived from passes.
